title: Bloom IELTS Academy — the school for English, accepted all over the globe
meta_description: Prepare for IELTS, TOEFL, PTE, Duolingo, Cambridge or OET with former examiners. Free placement test, AI-marked writing and speaking labs, and a study plan built from your real level.

props.badge: New — Placement test now gives a CEFR level and a band per skill
props.headline: Reach your band with teachers who marked the real exam.
props.subhead: Bloom is an English school and a study platform in one. We start with a placement test that gives you an honest level, then build the plan, the practice and the feedback around whatever that test says you are weakest at.

props.heading: We prepare you for one exam, properly.
props.body: Not general English lessons with an exam bolted on. Every hour you spend with Bloom is aimed at a specific part of a specific paper, chosen because your own test results say that is where your marks are going.

cards.title: IELTS Academic & General
cards.body: Our core programme. Four skills, all question types, and the band descriptors read literally rather than paraphrased.

cards.title: TOEFL, PTE & Duolingo
cards.body: The same skills, different formats and different scoring. We teach the format explicitly, because that is where most points are lost.

cards.title: General & spoken English
cards.body: For students who need confident English for work, study or daily life rather than a certificate with a number on it.

cards.title: One-to-one tutoring
cards.body: Forty-five minutes with the teacher who specialises in the part you are stuck on. Same-day slots are usually available.

cards.title: Mock exams & marking
cards.body: Full sittings under real timing, marked against the official descriptors, with a score report you could hand to a university.

cards.title: OET & medical English
cards.body: The Occupational English Test for doctors, nurses, dentists, pharmacists and other healthcare professionals — delivered with Future MedsAcademy.

cards.title: Applications & entries
cards.body: We book your test, check your documents and tell you honestly whether you are ready to sit it yet.

props.heading: Founded in 2025, in three countries at once.
props.body: Bloom began as three separate teaching practices — one in Muscat, one in Milan and one in Shanghai — run by examiners who kept meeting the same problem: students who understood English but could not show it under exam conditions. In 2025 the three merged and moved their operations to Bengaluru, India, where the academy is now headquartered.

cards.title: Milan, Italy

steps.title: Placement test
steps.body: Twenty-five minutes across grammar, vocabulary, reading, listening, writing and speaking. It returns a CEFR level, a band per skill, and your strongest and weakest areas — from what you actually did, not from what you told us.

steps.title: Your English profile
steps.body: An honest picture: where you sit on the CEFR scale, what your estimated band is on every exam scale, and which first-language errors we will be watching for as a speaker of your language.

steps.title: A plan built from it
steps.body: A day-by-day schedule to your test date, weighted towards your weakest skill, with a mock every Saturday and a checkpoint every fortnight. Tick each block off as you do it.

steps.title: Practice with real feedback
steps.body: Write an essay, get a band against all four descriptors and every error explained. Record a cue card, get fluency, vocabulary, grammar and pronunciation scored separately. Your recurring mistakes are collected into an error bank.

steps.title: Measured, then adjusted
steps.body: Every scored activity moves your estimate. When a mock says your reading is the problem, next week's plan changes. You always know what to revise today and what you have already mastered.

props.heading: Everything a serious candidate needs, in one place.

features.title: The School
features.body: Class notes, printable PDFs, audio drills and video lectures — all filed under Listening Part 4, Writing Task 1 and the thirteen other parts of the exam.

features.title: Writing Lab
features.body: Write under exam timing, get a band per criterion, sentence-level corrections, a model answer and a persistent error bank.

features.title: Speaking Lab
features.body: Parts 1, 2 and 3 with a real preparation timer, recording, and analysis of fluency, filler words, idiomatic range and grammar.

features.title: Vocabulary engine
features.body: 570 band-tagged words across nine essay topics, with six study modes and spaced repetition that schedules itself.

features.title: Grammar Academy
features.body: Twelve lessons — concept, real IELTS examples, then a test — ordered so the errors most common for your first language come first.

features.title: Bloom Tutor
features.body: Knows your level, your target, your weakest skill and every error pattern in your writing — so its advice is specific, never generic.

props.heading: This is what you log into every day.
props.body: Not a video library with a login. A working platform that knows your level, marks your work and decides what you study today.

staff.name: Meriam Friaa
staff.bio: Runs everything that is not a lesson — admissions, timetabling, teacher allocation, exam entries and the FMA Overseas partnership. Rebuilt the academy around measurement rather than goodwill; retention went from 71% to 94%.

staff.name: Dr. Sarah Whitfield
staff.role: Former IELTS Examiner · Listening & Reading Lead
staff.bio: Fourteen years marking IELTS Listening and Reading. Specialises in students who understand the content but lose marks on transfer and timing.

staff.name: Dr. Elena Marchetti
staff.bio: Trains IELTS writing examiners. Marks your essay against the official descriptors line by line, then rewrites one paragraph with you so you can see the difference.

staff.name: Michael Chen
staff.bio: Full mock interviews under exam conditions with immediate criterion-by-criterion feedback. Particularly strong on pronunciation for Mandarin, Cantonese and Vietnamese speakers.

staff.name: James Okonkwo
staff.bio: Reading strategy specialist. If you understand the passages but never finish the paper, this is the teacher to book.

staff.name: Anjali Prasad
staff.bio: Works almost exclusively with Hindi, Urdu, Bengali and Tamil speakers. Targets articles, tense consistency and the direct-translation habits that cap students at Band 6.

staff.name: Dr. Hana Al-Balushi
staff.bio: Leads the medical track for doctors, nurses and dentists sitting OET or the IELTS 7.0-each requirement for GMC, NMC and DHA registration.

staff.name: Li Wei
staff.bio: Focuses on the obstacles specific to Mandarin and Cantonese speakers: final consonants, plural and past-tense endings, and extending answers past one sentence.

props.heading: Where they started, and where they got to.

students.name: Priya Sharma
students.quote: I had taken IELTS twice and got 6.0 for writing both times without ever understanding why. Bloom marked my first essay against the four criteria and the problem was obvious in ten minutes.

students.name: Li Chen
students.quote: My reading comprehension was fine — I just never finished the paper. James timed my skim and taught me to locate rather than read. That single change was worth a band.

students.name: Aisha Khan
students.quote: I needed 7.0 in every band for nursing registration and speaking was holding me back. Michael showed me I was stopping at seventy seconds in Part 2.

props.eyebrow: Study abroad · in partnership with FMA Overseas
props.heading: A band is not the goal. The offer letter is.
props.body: Getting Band 7 is half the journey. Turning it into a place at a university abroad — the application, the credential check, the visa, the accommodation — is the other half. That is what FMA Overseas does, and Bloom students go straight through to them.

lockup.note: Your Bloom score report transfers directly into an FMA Overseas application file. One team, one set of documents, no repeating yourself.

items.title: Reach your band
items.body: Bloom gets you to the score your target university requires — including any per-skill minimum, which is where most applications actually fail.

items.title: Shortlist with FMA
items.body: An FMA Overseas counsellor matches your band, transcript and budget against real entry requirements and tells you where you will get in.

items.title: Apply and get offers
items.body: Applications, statements of purpose, credential evaluation and reference chasing, handled for you. Multiple offers, not one hopeful punt.

items.title: Visa and finance
items.body: Student visa filing, financial documentation, tuition deposits and the interview preparation that decides a UKVI or SEVIS outcome.

items.title: Arrive settled
items.body: Accommodation, airport pickup, bank account, registration and a Bloom alumni contact already studying on your campus.

checklist.title: Everything between your result and your first lecture.

items.title: Requirement checking before you sit
items.body: We confirm the exact overall and per-skill minimum your shortlist demands, so you do not pass the test and still miss the offer.

items.title: Credential evaluation
items.body: Degree and transcript assessment for the UK, Ireland, Canada, Australia, Germany and Italy — including ECTS conversion.

items.title: Pathway and foundation routes
items.body: If your band is not there yet, a pre-sessional English or foundation route that still leads to the same degree.

items.title: Scholarship and funding search
items.body: Merit awards, regional bursaries and assistantships matched to your profile — most students never find these alone.

items.title: Visa filing and interview prep
items.body: Financial evidence, the credibility interview, and the English-language part of the visa rules that changes most often.

items.title: One file, both teams
items.body: Your Bloom band history, mock reports and score conversions attach to your FMA application automatically.
